en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Propped-Up (Khambhakatavagga) 24. The Second Training Rule on Being Veiled.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group of six monks sat down in inhabited areas with their heads covered. ... [Omitted] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not sit down in an inhabited area with my head covered.
One must not sit down in an inhabited area with one's head covered."
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area with his head covered, commits an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
For one who has entered upon the rains-retreat,
for one in times of distress, and for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first offender":
thus ends the fourth training rule.
